### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **65** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/number-comparand-declared-type-door.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**36** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/number-comparand-declared-type-door.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 81 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c503c6205f762507cc3392b61e04cce8e6b21c8d` — the merge of head `2d2eaa736f3aac2c82e6f4c508b7325b6f2497fc` into base `63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c503c6205f762507cc3392b61e04cce8e6b21c8d && git checkout c503c6205f762507cc3392b61e04cce8e6b21c8d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7 2d2eaa736f3aac2c82e6f4c508b7325b6f2497fc && git checkout -B drift-repro 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7 && git merge --no-ff 2d2eaa736f3aac2c82e6f4c508b7325b6f2497fc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cad68d0754beee8adf7ded1e4b6842238ba0a0a0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine-find.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-nested-relation-lowering.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-query-lowering.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/number-comparand-declared-type-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/query-expression-conformance.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/relation-condition-prescription-cap.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/relation-filter-lowering.ts, packages/objectql/src/relation-semi-join.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-nested-relation-filter.test.ts, packages/rest/src/data-nested-object-door.test.ts, packages/rest/src/data-nested-relation-permission.test.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/crossobject-conjunct-refusal.test.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/cross-object-where.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-security-resolvers.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-middleware-and-context.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-internal-helpers.ts, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-filter.ts, packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/odata-driver.ts, packages/spec/src/data/readable-ids.ts, packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs (cited code, read at this head, not reviewed; the prose faces `.changeset/33626-relation-semi-join.md` and the two `content/docs` pages were read against the code and are judged in ④)

### ① Derived judgments

Read: card #33626 with its two rulings (Q1 comment 6889549817, Q2 comment 6889543194), the PR body and comments, the net diff of `c87e2ad2` to `cad68d07` by `git diff` / `git show`, and the code the hunks cite. Nothing built or run.

- **The declaration line does not declare the narrowing.** `Clause-②: yes (widening; narrowing on a related object …)` is read by `readClause2Line` (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `readArmToken`) as value `yes`, arm `widening`: the arm is the FIRST token inside the parenthesis, and everything after it is the seat's argument, which no reader reads. So the two narrowings exist only as prose. Every gate that keys on the arm sees none: `breakingDeclaration` in `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` pushes no `clause-②-narrowing` signal, so no ADR-0087 disposition and no migration is asked of the changeset; `reviewFace` in `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` answers the `declaration` face, not the `narrowing` one. The closed spelling for a diff that widens one surface and narrows another is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (the file's own table of four combinations). The changeset carries the same line byte for byte, so it has the same defect; its body has no `**BREAKING**` banner, no ADR-0087 disposition marker and no FROM / TO line for either narrowing. This is M1.
- **What moved, against the id-reading path on the merge base.** Previously refused, now answered: more than 1,000 matching related records on a single-valued relation on `find` / `findOne` / `count` / `aggregate`; a second and third relationship; in analytics a dotted `where` leaf of two or three hops and a cross-object leaf in a compiled dataset's own `filter`. All declared. Previously answered, now refused, and declared (in prose only, see M1): a related object on another datasource (`INVALID_FILTER` / 400, `relationSemiJoinDatasourceError`); a read whose driver compiles no composed leaf (MongoDB, OData: the driver's ADR-0139 D3 refusal, `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500).
- **Previously answered, now refused, and NOT declared (M3).** The site is now a `ReadableIds` leaf, so the executor boundary's `refuseUncomposableReadableIdsClasses` (`engine-security-resolvers.ts`) judges the related object on every site, planned or not, and refuses one that has an object-keyed middleware (`hasObjectMiddleware`) with ADR-0139 D5.2's `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500. On the merge base the lowering produced a plain id list, no leaf reached the boundary, and the id read simply ran that middleware: the request was served. In this tree that class is `sys_comment` and `sys_comment_reaction` (`plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts`) plus any object a host keys a middleware to through the public `registerMiddleware(fn, { object })`. The refusal text is written for the author of a leaf ("Read this class through its bounded probe, chosen before the leaf is written"), not for someone who wrote a filter, and a 500 gives a query author nothing to fix. The PR body names this in its acceptance notes as "still refused"; against `main` it is newly refused. The changeset, the docs and the declaration line do not carry it.
- **Ruling Q2 is not met by this head (M4).** The ruling on the card: MongoDB and OData are refused in the engine, before the driver, `INVALID_FILTER` / 400, "not the current `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 from inside the driver", and "the PR carries an ADR-0139 amendment". This head ships exactly the 500 the ruling replaced, moves the ruled behaviour to #33876, and still says `Fixes #33626`. The card's item 3 ("refuse with a stable code naming the reason") is unmet for the same reason. A driver outside this repository that implements neither the compile nor the D3 refusal now receives a non-list `$in` comparand from any caller's filter, where before only a security-authored leaf could reach it; with no capability bit the engine cannot tell.
- **The semi-join's bounding by the related object's rules.** Row scope and the filter-oracle field check: carried, because the related read runs its whole predicate pipeline as the caller and the captured `where` is what the driver would have been handed; the leaf keeps its identity through the outer pipeline (no code rebuilds a leaf; a clone loses the brand and is refused, never composed unscoped); `count`, `aggregate`, `findOne` and the `count` fallback all reach `composeReadableIdsAtBoundary`. A planned read that never reached its driver call composes to `$in: []`. Two rules are NOT carried as the id read carried them: M2 and S1 below. Under the public-repo rule the record states the rule only; the mechanism is handed to the seat.
- **Negation and NULL.** `$ne` inside the condition is the related object's own lowering and an absent or unreadable parent excludes the row, as documented. `$not` around a relation site admits a row whose parent is absent or unreadable, as it did over the id list on the merge base (no change; the analytics path refuses that shape by name, the data path serves it). A multi-valued relation at any hop, and `update` / `delete`, keep the capped id read: `site.multiple` is read per site, and the inner hop's own `find` decides for the inner hop.
- **Analytics.** `lowerCrossObjectWhere` respells up to three hops and checks every joined hop against its declared reference; the dataset `filter` takes the same reader through `servedScope`; a leaf left dotted keeps the dataset-filter refusal. The echo refusal `crossObjectEchoRefused` still says the engine "matches … against the ids it returns, refusing a match past its cap", which this change makes false for the leaves it is printed for (S2).
- **SQL push-down.** The change moves evaluation into the database and removes an in-process id list; nothing is pulled back into process on a SQL driver.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql` patch, `@objectstack/service-analytics` patch, `Metadata-protocol: none`. No `major`. With the arm corrected to `(narrowing)` the level rule still allows `patch` for a non-protocol narrowing, but the changeset then owes its BREAKING carrier, its ADR-0087 disposition and the migration for each narrowing (M1). `none` is doubtful on one point: a compiled dataset's definition-level `filter` is metadata, and a cross-object leaf in it goes from refused to served, which is a new accepted value for a metadata author on `@objectstack/service-analytics` (S4).

Check-runs on `cad68d0754beee8adf7ded1e4b6842238ba0a0a0`, read from the API during this review: 61 runs, all completed; 41 success, 19 skipped, 1 cancelled (an earlier `Check Changeset` run, superseded; the two later `Check Changeset` runs are success). `Test Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and the three `PR-body guards` runs are success. None in progress, none failed. The green `Check Changeset` is consistent with M1: it reads arm `widening` and asks for nothing more.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No published schema and no governed path in the 19 files; `packages/spec` is untouched. The governed parts (skills text, the ADR-0139 capability bit) are split to #33875 and #33876, which is why M4 exists.
- `skills/objectstack-query` on `main` still teaches one level and 1,000 ids for every relation; stricter than the engine after this lands, named in the changeset, carried by #33875.
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx` states "with the tenant wall on both tables"; see M2.
- `RELATION_CONDITION_MAX_HOPS` (objectql) and `CROSS_OBJECT_WHERE_MAX_HOPS` (service-analytics) are two homes for one number, tied by a docblock only (N2).

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing itself, against the published behaviour on `main`: both declared narrowings take a served capability away at the consumer; neither makes a refusal the spec already stated real. `main`'s `query-syntax.mdx` and `data-engine.mdx` promise the related read "as the caller, then matches the field against the ids it returns", with no datasource or driver condition.

- `packages/objectql/src/relation-semi-join.ts`, `engine-find.ts`, `engine-query-lowering.ts`, `engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts`, `engine.ts` — the planned read and the module-private scope map hold against `composeReadableIdsChain` and `ReadableIds.compose` for row scope and field readability. They do not hold against the module's own sentence "a related record is in the subquery exactly when a direct read of the related object with this condition would return it" (M2, S1), nor against the boundary's D5.2 refusal (M3). When no security service is registered the boundary still logs "every such leaf is answered `$in: []`" for a read whose only leaves are planned and are in fact composed (N1).
- `packages/objectql/src/relation-filter-lowering.ts`, `number-comparand-declared-type-door.ts` — the recursive admission is bounded at three, refuses at the inner path by name, and agrees with ADR-0071's limit and the card's item 1. `relationSemiJoinDatasourceError` is a clear 400, but the cross-datasource narrowing rests on no ruling: the card and both rulings speak of drivers, not of two datasources (S5).
- `packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/cross-object-where.ts`, `objectql-strategy.ts` — hold against the engine's nested form and the card's item 1; S2 for the stale echo copy.
- Tests (`engine-nested-relation-lowering.test.ts`, `query-expression-conformance.test.ts`, `relation-condition-prescription-cap.test.ts`, `data-nested-object-door.test.ts`, `data-nested-relation-permission.test.ts`, `analytics-nested-relation-filter.test.ts`, `crossobject-conjunct-refusal.test.ts`) — they pin hops, NULL ancestors, `$ne`, `$not`, row scope and the field check at the second hop. No added test pins either declared narrowing (the cross-datasource refusal, a non-compiling driver), the D5.2 refusal a filter author now meets, or the tenant wall on the subquery (S3).

Findings:

- M1 (must-fix) — The `Clause-②:` line on the PR body and the changeset reads `yes` / `widening`; the narrowing is unread prose. Write `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on both, and give the changeset its BREAKING carrier, its one ADR-0087 disposition marker and the FROM / TO fix for each narrowing.
- M2 (must-fix) — Security: the related object's tenant wall does not bound the subquery as it bounded the id read in every composition. Rule only; mechanism handed to the seat.
- M3 (must-fix) — Undeclared narrowing: a relation condition onto an object with an object-keyed middleware was served on `main` and is now refused `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 with ADR-0139 D5.2 wording. Serve it (the planned read ran that middleware), or refuse it `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 in a filter author's words, and declare whichever remains.
- M4 (must-fix) — Ruling Q2 on the card is unmet while the PR closes the card: MongoDB and OData go from served to the driver's 500 the ruling replaced. Land with #33876, or obtain the maintainer's word for the interim and change `Fixes` to `Part of`.
- S1 (should-fix) — Security: a read rule a related object applies after its driver call is not carried into the subquery. Rule only; mechanism handed to the seat.
- S2 (should-fix) — `crossObjectEchoRefused` still describes an id match and a cap; the card's item 5 asks for refusal copy updated.
- S3 (should-fix) — No test pins the cross-datasource refusal, the non-compiling-driver refusal, the D5.2 refusal at a filter, or the tenant wall on the subquery.
- S4 (should-fix) — `Metadata-protocol: none` beside a dataset `filter` that now accepts a cross-object leaf: declare `added` with `minor` on `@objectstack/service-analytics`, or state in the changeset why a dataset `filter` leaf is not a metadata author's accept set.
- S5 (should-fix) — The cross-datasource refusal takes a served request away with no ruling on the card; put it to the maintainer or cite the ruling that covers it.
- N1 (nit) — The "no usable security service" warning is logged, and its once-only slot spent, for a read whose leaves are all planned and composed.
- N2 (nit) — One hop limit, two constants in two packages.
